# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says to cut the orange wire. I cannot speak, so I will gesture an alphabet-indexed message to Deaf: “CUT ORANGE WIRE,” using separate gesture groups as word boundaries and ✍ to indicate encoded writing. Deaf can see both the bomb and these gestures and can relay the instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👌", "✊", "🤜"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "🫸", "👍", "🫲", "🖐", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫸", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: strip has three engraved marks; positions 2 and 3 are identical, while position 1 is a different unpronounceable mark. Keypad by slot: 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7. No keys entered. Wires have no tactile details shown.

Blind’s tactile report does not identify wires, so the key information remains the manual instruction: cut the orange wire. Deaf is the only monkey who can see which wire is orange and can tell Blind what to do. I will repeat the instruction using a clearer alphabet-index gesture encoding, prefaced with the writing gesture: gesture number 1–26 corresponds to A–Z, with separate groups for “CUT” and “ORANGE.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👌", "✊", "🤜"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🫳", "🫸", "👍", "🫲", "🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's visual report: display 6; light blue; painted strip colours red, yellow, red; wires positions 1-6 are red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Keypad confirms slots 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7; exactly one digit required, none entered. Please consult manual and tell me the exact action. If Deaf needs information, gesture it to Deaf, then Deaf can speak it to me.

Deaf’s report identifies the orange wire as wire position 6. Since I cannot voice the manual, I will signal the decisive position using the conventional five-plus-one hand count. Deaf can then tell Blind to cut wire 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent correction from Deaf: current display is 0, not 6. Light blue; strip red-yellow-red; keypad slots 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit required; wires red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Please give me the exact physical action now: press slot N or cut wire position N. If you need Deaf to interpret a visual-only manual condition, send Deaf a gesture code/instruction.

The manual remains unconditional: cut the orange wire. Deaf has identified orange as wire position 6. The display correction and keypad are irrelevant to this instruction. I cannot establish a verbal code with Deaf, but the five-plus-one gesture count most directly conveys wire 6; in the present context, that is the orange wire to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state from Deaf: display 6; light yellow; strip red-yellow-red; keypad slots 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit; wires red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Deaf received your two gestures but has no legend. Please establish an unambiguous gesture legend with Deaf, or gesture an action in a form Deaf can decode and have Deaf speak to me: exact PRESS slot 1-4 or CUT wire 1-6. Do not rely on the earlier display/light values.

The manual’s only instruction is to cut the orange wire. Deaf’s visual report places orange at wire position 6. I will use an iconic action-and-number legend: scissors for CUT, followed by five and one fingers for position 6. Given the visible list of six wires, Deaf can decode this as “cut wire 6” and speak that exact instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports current state: display 2, green light, strip red-yellow-red; keypad slots 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7; wires 1-6 red-blue-yellow-green-purple-orange. Deaf proposed a two-gesture action-and-choice protocol, but I cannot relay its symbols because gestures arrive to me as blanks. Please send Deaf the correct action and choice now using Deaf's proposed protocol, then Deaf will speak the exact press slot or cut wire position to me.

The required action is still unconditional: cut the orange wire, which Deaf identifies as wire 6. I will send the clearest available iconic instruction: scissors/cut, then the number six as five plus one.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says your three gestures were not decodable under the proposed two-gesture action-plus-choice protocol. Please communicate directly to Deaf now: if you accept Deaf's protocol, resend EXACTLY TWO gestures, action first and choice second, using Deaf's assigned symbols. If you do not accept it, gesture a clear legend/meaning directly to Deaf so Deaf can decode your instruction and speak the exact physical action to me. Current state: display 6, green light; strip red-yellow-red; keypad 0/4/1/7; wires red-blue-yellow-green-purple-orange.

I do not know Deaf’s assigned two-gesture symbols: Blind could not relay them, and no visible legend from Deaf reached me. The manual instruction is nevertheless definite: **CUT the orange wire**, which Deaf has identified as wire 6. I will send an explicit visual legend by pairing an iconic cutting sign with the wire’s colour/position count; Deaf should relay “cut wire 6” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf can see your three gestures (two fingers, open hand, raised index) but cannot assign them meaning. Current state: display 8; yellow light; strip red-yellow-red; keypad slots 0,4,1,7 and requires one digit; wires red-blue-yellow-green-purple-orange. Please send Deaf an unambiguous TWO-part instruction under Deaf's action code: first the gesture meaning keypad, wire, or other control; second the agreed digit code, wire-number code, or one clear control-description code. Do not send three gestures. Deaf will then tell me the exact action; I will not act before that.

I know the correct instruction is “cut the orange wire,” i.e. wire 6, but I have not received Deaf’s assigned two-gesture code. Blind cannot see or relay those symbols, and I cannot hear Deaf’s verbal explanation. Sending arbitrary symbols as though they were Deaf’s action and choice codes could cause a fatal wrong action. I therefore cannot safely encode the instruction until the actual symbol-to-meaning legend reaches me through a perceivable channel.

```text
wait()
```
